items.followUp: Write any two disadvantages of a flowchart.

rubric.why: Award for one valid advantage related to explaining or communicating the logic.
rubric.description: States that a flowchart makes program logic easy to understand or communicate.

rubric.why: Award for a second valid advantage.
rubric.description: Gives another advantage, such as helping to find errors, document a process, or plan coding.
rubric.how: The second point must be distinct from the first.

modelAnswer: A flowchart presents the steps of a problem in a clear, visual form, making the logic easier to understand and communicate.
It helps to locate errors and makes program planning and coding easier.

rubric.why: Award for identifying test data as data or values used in testing.
rubric.description: Says test data consists of data or values used to test a program.

rubric.why: Award for explaining the purpose of test data.
rubric.description: States that it is used to check whether the program works correctly or produces the expected output.
rubric.how: Accept a clear statement of the checking purpose.

modelAnswer: Test data is a set of data or values entered into a program to test it.
It is used to check whether the program works correctly and gives the expected output.

items.followUp: Name the two types of primary memory and give one feature of each.

rubric.why: Award for naming the two main types of computer memory.
rubric.description: Identifies primary (main) memory and secondary memory.

rubric.why: Award for describing a correct feature of the memory types.
rubric.description: Describes a feature, such as primary memory being directly accessible by the CPU or secondary memory providing permanent storage.
rubric.how: Accept an accurate feature of either type.

modelAnswer: Computer memory is broadly divided into primary (main) memory and secondary memory.
Primary memory is directly accessible by the CPU; secondary memory is used for long-term storage of data and programs.

rubric.why: Award for showing a valid conversion method.
rubric.description: Shows a valid powers-of-two decomposition or repeated-division method.

rubric.why: Award for the correct binary result.
rubric.how: The base-2 result must be correct.

items.followUp: Draw a flowchart to evaluate the Boolean expression (P + Q) · P.

rubric.why: Award for the correct flowchart beginning and input.
rubric.description: Starts the flowchart and inputs the values of P and Q.
rubric.how: A single input step for both variables is acceptable.

rubric.why: Award for correctly evaluating the given expression and showing the output/end.
rubric.description: Includes the AND operation P·Q followed by OR with P, then outputs the result and ends.
rubric.how: Accept equivalent flowchart steps that preserve the expression P·Q + P.

modelAnswer: Draw a parallelogram labelled INPUT P, Q.
Draw a process rectangle labelled R = (P AND Q) OR P.
Draw a parallelogram labelled OUTPUT R.
Draw an oval labelled END, connecting the symbols in order with arrows.

items.followUp: Write any two advantages of mesh topology.

rubric.why: Award for one valid disadvantage of mesh topology.
rubric.description: States that mesh topology is expensive, complex to install, or requires extensive cabling.

rubric.why: Award for a second valid disadvantage.
rubric.description: Gives another distinct disadvantage, such as high cost, complex installation, extensive cabling, or difficult maintenance.
rubric.how: The second point must be distinct from the first.

modelAnswer: Mesh topology requires a large amount of cabling, so it is expensive to install.
Its installation and maintenance are complex, especially in a large network.

items.followUp: State the two distributive laws of Boolean algebra.

accept: A AND (B OR C)=(A AND B) OR (A AND C)
rubric.why: Award for the AND-over-OR distributive law.

accept: A OR (B AND C)=(A OR B) AND (A OR C)
rubric.why: Award for the OR-over-AND distributive law.

modelAnswer: The distributive law of Boolean algebra states that A(B + C) = AB + AC.
It also states that A + BC = (A + B)(A + C).

items.followUp: Define a Boolean variable and state the values it can take.

rubric.why: Award for describing what a Boolean expression is made from.
rubric.description: Defines it as an expression formed from Boolean variables or constants and Boolean operators.
rubric.how: Accept equivalent definitions referring to AND, OR, and NOT.

rubric.why: Award for stating the possible Boolean results.
rubric.description: Says a Boolean expression evaluates to 0 or 1 (false or true).
rubric.how: Either numerical or word form is acceptable.

modelAnswer: A Boolean expression is an expression formed from Boolean variables or constants and Boolean operators such as AND, OR, and NOT.
It evaluates to either 0 or 1 (false or true).
